text: Of these zero and one, okay. So one and zero are the only possible bits that we can have, and we are processing, we are dealing with one at a time. That's binary modulation. And as I said, binary modulation means that you create one waveform for each bit. So one waveform carries one bit of information. That's binary modulation. Okay, that's already let's say useful, but there are let's say more efficient ways to create this process. What would be more efficient than that? It would be more efficient if for each signal that we create, we do not carry only one bit, but we carry more bits. Why is that more efficient? Because now we increase the amount of bits that we are carrying with a single signal. So we increase the so called bit rate because for each signal we are carrying more information, right? So we increase the speed with which we transfer bits. So if we are for example able to transfer with one signal three bits instead of one, it means that we increase the speed with which we transfer the bits by three times.
